_readme: Source of truth for every translatable string on the nine public marketing pages. The site never fetches this file at runtime: English is whatever the HTML already contains, and switching back to English restores the original markup. This file exists so the translated dictionaries have one authoritative English reference to work from. Keys ending in a value that contains HTML tags are applied with innerHTML, so the tags must be preserved in every translation.

In the Robotics Workshop, students get a drone, but no controller!

instructors.heading: Instructors
instructors.mission: Mission: Inspiring learners through hands-on engineering workshops
instructors.body: At Stage One Education, we offer workshops that capture the expertise and practices of top researchers and engineering professionals. Our workshops are led by a nationwide network of experienced instructors who guide participants through immersive, hands-on, project-based learning reflecting the latest engineering fields. This dynamic approach provides an experience powered by the insights and passion of real-world engineers.

Our hands-on workshops in Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Mechanical Engineering are led by real engineers. In just three hours, participants gain essential skills and tools that ignite their passion for STEM.

about.heading: About Us

intro.headline: We're dedicated to sharing our love of engineering
intro.body1: through hands-on activities—from building real circuits to working with professional-grade CAD tools and the latest AI models—participants gain a true sense of what engineering is all about.
intro.body2: After engaging with real-world projects, engineering tools, and talking to experienced professionals, participants walk away more confident, inspired, and excited about their potential future in engineering.

andy.name: Andrew Barry, MIT Ph.D.
andy.bio: Andy fell in love with autonomous drones by flying them for his Ph.D. at MIT. Andy has brought electronics and software workshops to over 10,000 students, from small helicopters to sophisticated quadrupeds.

pete.name: Pete Florence, MIT Ph.D.
pete.bio: Pete flew drones of all sorts during his Ph.D. work at MIT. His planning and control work in the Robot Locomotion Group pushed the horizons for faster, more agile, and more reliable drones. His award-winning robot manipulation research is giving robots new abilities every day.

robbie.name: Robbie Kipp, Engineer
robbie.bio: Robbie's engineering designs set the course for the future of dive systems and maritime vessels during his time as an ocean engineer and naval architect. Now, as the Director of Operations at Stage One Education, he pioneers innovative approaches to inspire the next generation of engineers. Robbie is an avid diver, climber, and aviation enthusiast.
